report.answer_text:
In 2025, the Trump administration replaced every voting member of the CDC’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP), the panel that advises the CDC on who should receive vaccines and when. It kept the committee in place but changed its membership, leadership, and how outside medical groups could participate. (hhs.gov)
June: Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. removed all 17 sitting voting members on June 9 and named eight replacements on June 11, including several who had criticized COVID-19 vaccines or vaccination policy. HHS said the overhaul was meant to address conflicts of interest and restore public trust; the American Medical Association questioned the transparency and vetting of the new appointments. (hhs.gov)
Summer and fall: Nonvoting liaisons from outside medical organizations were excluded from ACIP’s evidence-review workgroups in their capacity as organizational representatives. HHS announced five more appointees on September 15. By December, Kirk Milhoan had succeeded Martin Kulldorff as chair, with Robert Malone serving as vice chair. (ama-assn.org)
The reconstituted panel voted to shift COVID-19 vaccination from a routine recommendation to individual decisions with a clinician and to end the routine hepatitis B birth-dose recommendation for infants whose mothers tested negative. On March 16, 2026, a federal judge temporarily stayed 13 appointments and all committee votes taken after June 11, 2025. (everycrsreport.com)
